extracted.intended_audience: students and readers interested in American political parties and party organization (political science audience, general educated public)
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory account of the aims, structure, and procedures of American political party organizations (committees, primaries, conventions) and how candidates are selected and parties exercised power. Focuses on practical functions and historical/practical advantages of the American system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union
rubrics_metrics.description: to keep the party together and prevent it from wasting its strength by dissensions and schisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the primary aims of a party organization (particularly important to a European politician observing American practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruiting
rubrics_metrics.description: to bring in new voters, e.g. immigrants when they obtain citizenship, young men as they reach the age of suffrage, new-comers, or residents hitherto indifferent or hostile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an explicit aim of party organizations; recruitment is a central, measurable activity (targeting specific groups as they attain suffrage or relocate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enthusiasm
rubrics_metrics.description: to excite the voters by the sympathy of numbers and the sense of a common purpose, rousing them by speeches or literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Party organizations are expected to mobilize emotions and collective identity through rhetoric and printed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: to give the voters some knowledge of the political issues they have to decide, to inform them of the virtues of their leaders, and the crimes of their opponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties have an educative function—disseminating information about issues and candidates; this can be explicit (tracts, speeches) and is named separately from mere enthusiasm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of party candidates (the mainspring)
rubrics_metrics.description: the selection of party candidates is the mainspring of the whole mechanism; important because elective places are numerous and tenable for short terms, so elections frequently recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why candidate selection often outranks the other aims: parties exist practically to fill offices and carry on machinery of government; thus nomination rules and practices are central to party purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three methods of bringing candidates before electors
rubrics_metrics.description: One: candidate offers himself appealing to personal merits; Two: a group or junto of influential men puts a candidate forward; Three: the candidate is chosen by the people themselves (members of a party acting in mass or through representatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each method is described with historical and comparative notes; the third (selection by party membership/representatives) is presented as the system prevailing in America and as having specific advantages (secures good candidate, encourages candidates, secures party union).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative, bottom-to-top organization (essential feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential feature of the system is that it is from bottom to top strictly representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This representativeness is tied to the organization's power—only a representative body will be yielded power by the people; non-representative bodies (mere committees for canvassing) have little power. The account stresses theory: power must flow from the people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two distinct sets of bodies: permanent (managing committees) and temporary (nominating assemblies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization consists of two distinct but intimately connected sets of bodies: the permanent ones manage party business, the temporary ones nominate party candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This binary is foundational: managing committees handle ongoing administrative and campaign tasks, while primaries/conventions (temporary) perform nominations; the division of competence is emphasized (committees do not choose candidates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of managing committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing committees (at ward, township, city, county, State, National levels) raise and apply funds for election purposes and political agitation, organize meetings, prepare lists of voters, disseminate political tracts and information, look after the press, attend to admission of immigrants as citizens and their enrolment on party lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also supervise the canvass, procure and distribute tickets at polls (unless public authority does this), allot money for election services, ensure voters are brought to polls, and convoke nominating assemblies. They are permanent bodies, usually re-appointed annually, and often dominated by the same individuals (chairmen can be powerful).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of committee competence: choice of candidates belongs to nominating assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: One function and one only — besides that of adopting platforms — is beyond the competence of these committees: the choice of candidates. That belongs to the nominating assemblies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies institutional separation: committees manage and prepare, but nominations are made by primaries or conventions (temporary bodies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary: composition and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary is composed of all the party voters resident within the bounds of the township or ward; it has two duties: (1) to select candidates for its own local district offices, and (2) to elect delegates to nominating meetings (conventions) of larger areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primaries are feasible for small local units where voters can meet; for larger areas delegates are used. The primary's internal procedure (summons by local committee, submission and vote on names, chairman signs list of delegates) is described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating convention: composition and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A nominating convention is composed of delegates from all the primaries within its limits, chosen at those primaries for the sole purpose of selecting candidates; procedure includes temporary chairman, Committee on Credentials, election of a permanent chairman, proposals and votes on candidates, and sometimes adoption of resolutions or a platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions are used where the number of voters is too great for a single meeting; managing committees usually arrange nominees beforehand but any delegate may propose a candidate and the majority vote decides the nominee. Conventions then adjourn sine die.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of delegates and multiple conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary often sends delegates to multiple conventions (city, assembly district, senatorial district, congressional district, State convention etc.), because local units are nested within several different election districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the complexity and multiplicity of delegations: the same primary selects delegates for different nominating bodies according to overlapping jurisdictional levels; sometimes some nominating bodies may be primaries rather than conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages of selection by party membership/representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection by the people themselves (members of the party, mass or through representatives) promises to secure a good candidate because presumably the people will choose a suitable man; it encourages the candidate by giving him the weight of party support; it secures the union of the party because a previous vote determines majority preference and the minority are likely to fall into line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argumentative justification for the American practice of representative selection (primaries/conventions); ties into democratic theory and the idea that the ruling majority must name its standard-bearers to remain active rather than passive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating authorities: primaries vs conventions as the two sets
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule there are only two sets of nominating authorities: the primary which selects candidates for its own petty offices, and the convention composed of delegates from primaries for larger districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distills organizational forms into two practical kinds of nominating bodies; local variation and statutory changes are acknowledged but the typology is presented as the typical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal nature of primaries and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Primaries and conventions, unlike the local party associations of England, are convoked but once, make their nominations, and vanish; they are 'swans which sing their one song and die.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the temporary, episodic role of nominating bodies compared with permanent committees; national conventions (every four years) are a special case with longer lead time before elections.
